mss-416b221eb3865a6a4834.text:
Relaxation of a myocardial cell occurs when:

- Ca2+ is reaccumulated in the sarcoplasmic reticulum by the action of {{c1::Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA)}}
- Ca2+ is pumped out of the cell by the {{c2::Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (NCX)}}
mss-416b221eb3865a6a4834.extra:
- The Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA) is regulated by the protein phospholamban

- When unphosphorylated, phospholamban inhibits SERCA

- But when phosphorylated, phospholamban is itself inhibited; this leads to faster uptake of Ca2+ into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, thereby contributing to lusitropy (the rate of myocardial relaxation)

mss-6c2c2c593f5c811236a4.extra:
- These are strong vasodilators which increase blood flow, thus "sweeping" procoagulant factors out of the area; in pulmonary arterial hypertension there is endothelial dysfunction which leads to increased vasoconstrictors and decreased vasodilators

- PGI2 also blocks platelet aggregation (opposite of TXA2)

Endothelial cells prevent thrombosis through:

- Thrombomodulin: Redirects thrombin to activate protein C, inhibiting factors Va and VIIIa
- tPA: Converts plasminogen to plasmin, promoting fibrinolysis
- Prostacyclin (PGI2): Inhibits platelet aggregation and causes vasodilation
- Nitric oxide (NO): Inhibits platelet adhesion and promotes vasodilation
- Heparan sulfate: Enhances antithrombin III, inhibiting thrombin and factor Xa
- Barrier function: Blocks exposure to subendothelial collagen and tissue factor

- The {{c2::A}} band remains the same length
mss-db70c2a191af4e5ce51a.extra:
- The A band stays the sAme

- A single sarcomere is defined as the distance between two Z lines

- I band is the region of sarcomere with only thin filaments and are bound to structural proteins at the Z line
- A band corresponds to the thick filaments and includes portions overlapped by thin filaments

mss-15af2b97d23ee36236e2.text: Succinylcholine is a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker that binds to post-synaptic {{c1::ACh}} receptors, triggering an influx of Na+ and efflux of K+
mss-15af2b97d23ee36236e2.extra:
- Conditions that upregulate post-synaptic ACh receptors may lead to life-threatening hyperkalemia (e.g., skeletal muscle trauma, burn injury, stroke)

- Instead, use nondepolarizing blocking agents (vecuronium, rocuronium)

- MOA of succinylcholine: Sustained depolarization → unresponsive motor plate to subsequent impulses (more Na+ in, more K+ out)
